study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
outcome: composite maternal morbidity (maternal fever, postpartum hemorrhage, transfusion, endometritis, severe perineal lacerations)
composite neonatal morbidity (respiratory distress syndrome, mechanical ventilation, birth injury, seizures, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, therapeutic hypothermia, umbilical artery pH <= 7.1)
cohort: The study included 6,509 term gravidas who reached active labor (6 cm) between 2010 and 2015.
finding: A prolonged latent phase (PLP) (defined as >=90th percentile of labor duration) is associated with increased maternal morbidity in both induced and spontaneous labor, and with increased neonatal morbidity in spontaneous labor only.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery occurred more often in the PLP group, but the increased maternal morbidity associated with PLP was not mediated by cesarean delivery.
